content:
maria_support: heads-up — multiple customers reporting 504s and request timeouts on hosted inference for the last 12m. customer org 'acme-inc' hit a big spike. p95 request latency jumping from ~200ms -> 6s and a bunch of 5xx. sample req id: r-q7f9d. :eyes:

jake_oncall: on it. seeing gateway 504s in the dashboard too. can you paste the common request id and a top-level timeframe?

maria_support: pasted r-q7f9d above, window 2026-03-17T14:12->14:24Z. support ticket #S-7834. customer says calls that used to be fast now intermittently timeout.

dmitri_sre: checking batcher and queue metrics. initial glance: continuous-batcher pending_queue_depth spiked and never recovered; dequeue rate flat. possible queue saturation.

infra-bot: alert: hosted-gateway queue_depth > 95% for pool hosted-eu-west-1 (nodes: 8) — triggering backpressure.

jake_oncall: logs show repeated "RequestBufferFullError" from request-muxer and batcher warnings: 
```
WARN batcher: pending queue size=1580 max=1600 backlog_ms_avg=4200
ERROR router: reject request id=r-q7f9d reason=RequestBufferFull
```

rahul_eng: that looks like continuous batching backlog. likely cold-paths building up KV-cache warming or long-running requests blocking batchers. did the customer send any long sequences or streaming?

maria_support: customer says they sent some long chat histories (20k tokens) and a small subset of calls hitting heavy instruction tuning. but the 5xx spread across short calls too.

rahul_eng: two hypotheses: 1) long requests are occupying execution slots -> reduces throughput -> queue piles up. 2) a regression in our batch-split/eviction logic causing stuck batchers.

sophia_platform: temp mitigation: enable per-tenant request-throttling and set fallback routing for acme-inc to model-variant=small for 10m. that should drop mean latency and let queues drain. we can also enable adaptive-shedder to begin rejecting early.

jake_oncall: agreed. doing a rapid throttle now. @sophia_platform please apply fallback.

sophia_platform: applied route override for tenant acme-inc -> model: small-v1, and enabled burst_limit=20/min. watch for errors.

maria_support: customer confirms reduced 5xx after 90s. still seeing occasional timeouts but much lower. thanks.

rahul_eng: let's reproduce locally: steps I used: 
1) spin up a small hosted-like env with 4 batchers, max_pending=1600, continuous_batcher.window_ms=20.
2) send mixed traffic: 5% long 15k-token requests (exec time ~6s) and 95% short 30-100 token requests at steady 600rps.
3) observe pending queue growth and 504s when pending > max_pending.

rahul_eng: repro logs snippet: 
```
INFO worker[0]: started exec req=r-abc duration=6.1s tokens=15000
WARN batcher: combine_time=19ms pending=1200 dequeue_rate=180/s
ERROR router: deadline exceeded for req=r-xyz status=504
```

dmitri_sre: interestingly, the monitors show a sudden drop in dequeue_rate around the same time a GC pause spike occurred on one of the GPU host processes. could be exacerbating blockage.

jake_oncall: which config knobs to change to mitigate without full rollback?

rahul_eng: short-term (minutes): 
- reduce continuous_batcher.max_pending from 1600 -> 800 (lowers memory pressure).
- reduce continuous_batcher.window_ms from 20 -> 10 to favor latency over batching.
- enable adaptive-shedder to reject extreme bursts (early reject).
- route noisy tenants to small-variant fallback like @sophia did.

sophia_platform: ops note: lowering max_pending requires rollout across pool; I'll do rolling config change on hosted-eu-west-1 pool.

infra-bot: deploy plan queued: change continuous_batcher.max_pending=800 on pool hosted-eu-west-1 -> rolling restart batcher pods (max 2 at a time). ETA 6m.

jake_oncall: proceed. monitor p95 and pending queue.

maria_support: meanwhile, customer asked for root cause and ETA. I'd like to give an update: applied temporary fallback, throttling enabled, queued infra mitigation (rolling config update). ETA ~10–15m for stabilization.

dmitri_sre: we should also check KV-cache warmup path: if many cold-model loads cause long CPU-bound model loads on startup, they can bury batcher. check model-load times: 
```
model-loader: load_time_ms model=huge-v2 t=4312
model-loader: load_time_ms model=small-v1 t=88
```
If cold loads align with spike, we need prewarm policies for large-model variants.

rahul_eng: follow-up actions for postmortem: 
- add kvcache/prewarm for large models (timebox).
- add per-tenant burst controls to default routing policy.
- improve observability: per-batch occupancy and dequeue latencies on dashboard.
- test restart/backpressure behavior under mixed long/short workload in chaos lab.

jake_oncall: current metrics after change: pending queue dropped from 1500 -> 320 in 3m, p95 reduced to 420ms, 504 rate down 92%. Good.

maria_support: customer emailed back: major volume restored, still watching. They asked if we can prevent recurrence. told them next steps and postmortem will be shared.

sophia_platform: adding postmortem action items to backlog and assigning owners: kvcache-prewarm -> @rahul_eng, per-tenant-burst-limits -> @sophia_platform, observability gaps -> @dmitri_sre.

support-bot: ticket S-7834 updated: mitigation applied, customer notified, status: monitoring.

maria_support: closing the escalation for now, will update again if anything flares. great cross-team response, thanks everyone :heart:
